task.description:
Validate REQ-198's design (lib/letflow/design/req198-expr-builtin-functions.md) -- the function-call syntax form and 8 pure builtin functions (length, lower, upper, trim, contains, startsWith, endsWith, coalesce) atop REQ-197's just-shipped arithmetic/precedence/structured-error extension to lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex. Read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-198 entry in full yourself before validating -- do not trust this summary alone.

The design's key claims, for you to independently re-verify against the real expr.ex (post-REQ-197, current main/branch state), not just against this design doc's own prose:
1. Lex-time closed whitelist (design section 1): identifier_token/1 and identifier_token_kv/1 (the two existing 6-clause identifier-classification functions at expr.ex ~L360-367 and ~L667-674) each gain one new clause classifying exactly 8 literal names (length, lower, upper, trim, contains, startsWith, endsWith, coalesce) as a new {:builtin_call, name} token kind, inserted before the existing catch-all {:var, ...} clause. now/date_add/date_diff are deliberately NOT added to the whitelist.
2. 'Identifier followed by ( is a hard parse error' (design section 1.2) is claimed to already be TRUE TODAY with zero new code, via parse_primary/1's existing {:var, path} clause leaving a following {:lparen} token unconsumed, which propagates to the existing trailing_input rejection. Verify this claim by reading parse_primary/1 (expr.ex ~L937-950) and parse/1's outer with-clause yourself -- confirm the trailing-input mechanism really does fire for e.g. now(1) or frobnicate(1) with no new rejection code required.
3. New AST node {:call, builtin_name(), args :: [ast()]} (design section 2), grammar production at the parse_primary level requiring {:builtin_call, name} immediately followed by {:lparen}.
4. Semantics tables (design section 3) for all 8 functions: length byte-length via byte_size/1 with null propagation and non-string type-mismatch error; ASCII-only lower/upper (DECIDED in section 3.2.1, with reasoning -- verify the decision is actually stated, not left open, and that concrete non-ASCII test values are given, e.g. lower("CAFE with accent") behavior); trim stripping the same 4-byte ASCII whitespace set do_tokenize/2 already uses; contains/startsWith/endsWith with either-argument-null-yields-null; coalesce variadic >=1 arg, first non-null else null.
5. Arity checking (design section 4): fixed-arity functions (length/lower/upper/trim: exactly 1; contains/startsWith/endsWith: exactly 2) and coalesce (>=1, variadic) checked immediately after argument evaluation, before per-function semantics -- produces a NEW :wrong_arity eval-error reason tag, added to the existing {:eval_error, {tag, ...}} family.
6. @unsupported_call_markers collision check (design section 5): the design quotes the REAL, CURRENT 17-entry list read directly from expr.ex (~L129-147) and argues none of the 8 new builtin-call-syntax strings (especially "contains(" and "startsWith(", called out by name in the requirement text) collides with or weakens any existing marker. Re-verify this against the actual list in expr.ex yourself, not just against the design's quoted copy -- confirm the design's quoted list matches the real file exactly.
7. Dual error-surface reuse (design section 6): arity/type errors surface through eval/2's existing {:error, {:eval_error, reason}} shape (no new outer shape); a call to an UNRECOGNIZED name is a parse_strict/1 structured PARSE error (AC2), while a call to a RECOGNIZED name with WRONG ARITY is an eval_error (AC3) -- these are deliberately different error classes, both explicitly reusing REQ-197's existing dual mechanism rather than inventing a second one. Verify this split is coherent and matches AC2 vs AC3's actual wording in docs/requirements.yaml.
8. Purity re-verification procedure (design section 7): exact grep command reused verbatim from REQ-197's moduledoc, confirmation that byte_size/1, String.downcase/upcase(s, :ascii), String.contains?/starts_with?/ends_with?, and a plain left-to-right nil-scan are all pure with no clock/Repo/Logger/File/HTTP/:rand/:crypto dependency.
9. Non-goals (design section 8) and 2 flagged low-risk open questions (design section 9, OQ-1 trim's exact whitespace byte set, OQ-2 contains/startsWith/endsWith byte-vs-codepoint semantics) -- both explicitly non-blocking, not gating ELIXIR-DEV's implementation, unlike REQ-197's own OQ-1 which WAS blocking. Confirm neither open question here is actually load-bearing enough that it should have been escalated as blocking instead.

Also verify, independently of the design doc's own claims: zero literal Elixir implementation code anywhere in the design doc (grep for 'defmodule', 'def ', a trailing bare 'end' outside a @type/@spec continuation) -- every fenced block must be a @type/@spec declaration, a table, BNF, or plain-English pseudocode, never a working function body. This project has twice reworked REQ-197's own design doc for exactly this defect (commits 3680243, 290c6b2) -- check this design doc did not repeat it.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-198's 11 acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml) maps to a concrete design element -- cross-check the design's own section 10 traceability table against the real acceptance_criteria list yourself rather than trusting the table's accuracy.

The lex-time whitelist mechanism (section 1) is confirmed against the REAL current expr.ex source (identifier_token/1, identifier_token_kv/1, parse_primary/1, parse_primary_p/2) -- not merely internally consistent with the design doc's own prior sections.

The @unsupported_call_markers list quoted in section 5 is byte-for-byte identical to the real list in expr.ex (currently ~L129-147) -- re-grep it yourself, do not trust the design doc's transcription.
The ASCII-vs-Unicode case-conversion decision (section 3.2.1) is a genuine DECISION with reasoning and concrete test values, not left open or hedged.

The arity-checking design (section 4) correctly handles coalesce's variadic >=1 requirement distinctly from the other 7 functions' fixed arities, and the :wrong_arity eval-error reason fits the existing {:eval_error, {tag, ...}} family without changing eval/2's outer @spec shape.

The AC2-vs-AC3 error-class split (section 6) -- unrecognized name is a parse error, recognized name with wrong arity is an eval error -- is coherent and does not invent a second, competing error-surfacing mechanism beyond what REQ-197 already established.

EE-05's catch-false contract is confirmed intact for a wrong-arity or unrecognized-call gateway condition, via evaluate_condition/2's existing unconditional catch-false composition, with no new branch added.

Zero literal Elixir implementation code anywhere in the design doc -- grep for 'defmodule', 'def ', and a trailing bare 'end' outside a @type/@spec continuation; confirm every fenced block remains a @type/@spec declaration, table, BNF, or plain-English pseudocode.

now()/date_add()/date_diff() are confirmed NOT added to the whitelist, and the rejection mechanism for calls to them is confirmed to be the existing trailing-input parse-error path, not a new explicit rejection clause.

CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (this file, top level, not nested under result) must be exactly one of PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish your pass -- grep the file yourself before finishing, and run mix letflow.lint_handoffs if available, per this project's own recurring anti-pattern entry on this exact mistake.
